## Scope

This note documents the first CRAN-readiness remediation pass after running:

- `R CMD build .`
- `R CMD check --as-cran NGeoTrack_0.1.1.tar.gz`

It captures each warning/note, its source, and the most direct fix.
It also documents the risky replacement of `tidyr::pivot_wider()` in `check_overlap()` with base `stats::reshape()` and validates output shape with a minimal reproducible example.

## Risky Change Validation: `reshape` Replacing `pivot_wider`

The goal is to preserve the same effective wide output used by `check_overlap()`:

- one row per lower-level cluster (`botID`)
- exactly two top-level columns each for ID and name
- output columns in this order:
  - `botID`, `topID_1`, `topID_2`, `topName_1`, `topName_2`

```{r reshape-validation}
# Minimal joint-key-like input with one overlapping lower-level cluster.
# The overlap must happen within the same year for the same botID.
df_key_min <- data.frame(
  geoID = c(101001, 101002, 101003, 202001),
  Gname = c("A1", "A2", "A3", "B1"),
  Gcluster_id = c(5001, 5001, 5001, 5002),
  year = c(2019, 2019, 2019, 2019),
  mun_id = c(301, 302, 302, 401),
  Cname = c("Mun X", "Mun Y", "Mun Y", "Mun Z"),
  Ccluster_id = c(7001, 7002, 7002, 8001),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
attr(df_key_min, "comment") <- "grunnkrets-kommune"

# Internal shape used by check_overlap().
internal <- df_key_min
colnames(internal) <- c("geoID", "botName", "botID", "year", "topgeoID", "topName", "topID")

test_long <- internal |>
  dplyr::group_by(botID, year) |>
  dplyr::mutate(n_Top = length(unique(topID))) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::filter(n_Top != 1) |>
  dplyr::select(c(botID, topID, topName, year)) |>
  dplyr::distinct(botID, topID, topName, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::group_by(botID, topID) |>
  dplyr::mutate(max_year = max(year)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::filter(max_year == year) |>
  dplyr::select(-c(year, max_year)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(botID) |>
  dplyr::mutate(name = seq_len(dplyr::n())) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  as.data.frame()

# Base R replacement for tidyr::pivot_wider().
wide_base <- test_long[order(test_long$botID, test_long$name), , drop = FALSE]
wide_base <- stats::reshape(
  wide_base,
  idvar = "botID",
  timevar = "name",
  direction = "wide"
)
wide_base <- wide_base[, c("botID", "topID.1", "topID.2", "topName.1", "topName.2"), drop = FALSE]
colnames(wide_base) <- c("botID", "topID_1", "topID_2", "topName_1", "topName_2")
row.names(wide_base) <- NULL

# Expected contract for this minimal case.
expected <- data.frame(
  botID = 5001,
  topID_1 = 7001,
  topID_2 = 7002,
  topName_1 = "Mun X",
  topName_2 = "Mun Y",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

stopifnot(identical(wide_base, expected))
wide_base
```

Optional confidence check against `tidyr::pivot_wider()` if installed locally:

```{r optional-tidyr-compare, eval=TRUE}
if (requireNamespace("tidyr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  wide_tidyr <- tidyr::pivot_wider(test_long, names_from = name, values_from = c(topID, topName))
  wide_tidyr <- wide_tidyr[, c("botID", "topID_1", "topID_2", "topName_1", "topName_2"), drop = FALSE]
  wide_tidyr <- as.data.frame(wide_tidyr)

  wide_base_cmp <- wide_base[order(wide_base$botID), , drop = FALSE]
  wide_tidyr_cmp <- wide_tidyr[order(wide_tidyr$botID), , drop = FALSE]
  row.names(wide_base_cmp) <- NULL
  row.names(wide_tidyr_cmp) <- NULL

  row.names(wide_tidyr) <- NULL
  stopifnot(identical(wide_base_cmp, wide_tidyr_cmp))
}
```
